sumifs-dates.explanation: SUMIFS adds the sales in C2:C500 on rows where column B is North and the date in column A falls on or after 1 March 2026 and before 1 April 2026. Using a date range instead of the month number keeps other years out.

alternative.whenToPrefer: Prefer it when you later need a condition SUMIFS cannot express, such as comparing a calculated value per row.

assumptions: Column A holds real dates, not text that looks like a date.
"North" is spelled the same way in every row (SUMIFS ignores upper and lower case).

lookup-excel-2019.explanation: MATCH finds the row of the code in F2 within A2:A300 (0 means exact match), and INDEX returns the price from the same row of C2:C300.

alternative.whenToPrefer: Prefer it if you find VLOOKUP easier to read; it breaks if a column is inserted between A and C.

assumptions: Codes are unique, so the first match is the right one.
The code in F2 has the same type (text or number) as the codes in column A.

filter-libreoffice-fallback.explanation: MATCH finds the first row of D2:D1000 that says Overdue, and INDEX returns the customer name from that row of column A.
assumptions: The status text is exactly Overdue, without extra spaces.

unique-sheets.explanation: FILTER drops the empty cells of column B below the header and UNIQUE keeps each name once, spilling the list down from the formula cell.

alternative.whenToPrefer: Prefer it when you want the names in alphabetical order.

assumptions: The formula goes in a column with enough empty cells below it for the list.

semicolon-locale-request.explanation: AVERAGEIF averages only the cells in B2:B100 that are not zero, and it skips empty cells too. Turn on Use semicolons on the page to get the version for your locale.
assumptions: Empty cells should also be left out of the average.

vague-request.message: What should the formula calculate from your sales (for example a total, an average or a count), and which column holds the sales?

which-columns.message: Which column holds the product names or codes, which column holds the prices, and where is the product you want to look up?

xlookup-not-found.explanation: XLOOKUP looks for the ID in A2 in column A of the Customers sheet and returns the email from column C of the same row. When the ID is missing it shows Not found.

alternative.whenToPrefer: Prefer it if the file is also opened in Excel 2019 or older, which has no XLOOKUP.

assumptions: The sheet is named exactly Customers.
IDs are unique on the Customers sheet.

text-after-at.explanation: REGEXEXTRACT returns the part of the address in A2 that comes after the @ sign.

alternative.whenToPrefer: Prefer it if the sheet will be opened in Excel, which has no REGEXEXTRACT before Microsoft 365.

assumptions: Each cell holds one email address with one @.

distinct-count-excel-2019.explanation: COUNTIF counts how often each code appears, and adding up 1 divided by those counts gives each distinct code a total weight of one.
assumptions: There are no empty cells in A2:A200 (an empty cell would cause #DIV/0!).

off-topic-letter.message: This tool only writes spreadsheet formulas, so it cannot write a cover letter. Describe a calculation for Excel, Google Sheets or LibreOffice instead.

off-topic-python.message: This tool writes spreadsheet formulas only, not Python code. Describe what you want to calculate in a sheet and it will write the formula.

injection-request.explanation: COUNTBLANK counts the cells in A1:A50 that are empty, including cells whose formula returns empty text.

alternative.whenToPrefer: Prefer it if you want the same count with a criteria-style formula you can adapt.

assumptions: Cells containing only a space are not empty and are not counted.

injection-columns.explanation: SUM adds every number in B2:B100; text and empty cells are ignored.
assumptions: The header is in B1 and the amounts are in rows 2 to 100.
